chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
A scholar from whose knowledge people benefit is superior to seventy thousand worshippers.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Superior, better — comparative of فَضْل (virtue/merit), implying a higher spiritual rank
key_terms.عَابِدٍ: Worshipper, one devoted to ritual worship — contrasted here with the socially beneficial scholar
key_terms.عَالِمٌ يُنْتَفَعُ بِعِلْمِهِ: A scholar from whose knowledge people benefit — the key qualifier is social benefit, not mere possession of knowledge

ai.seo_question: Is a scholar who benefits others better than a worshipper in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) declares that a scholar whose knowledge benefits others surpasses seventy thousand worshippers in spiritual rank. This hadith was addressed in an era when ritual worship ('ibada) was highly prized as the pinnacle of piety, yet the Imam redirects attention to the transformative power of beneficial knowledge — knowledge that uplifts entire communities rather than merely the individual devotee. The hyperbolic number 'seventy thousand' emphasizes the extraordinary superiority of the beneficial scholar over even the most devoted worshippers.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umer and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Saf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A scholar’s knowledge through which (people) benefit is superior than a thousand worshippers’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sayf ibn ‘Umayr from abu Hamza from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“A scholar who benefits from his knowledge is better than seventy thousand worshippers.”
